The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 794bf524061c4b36), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 198. statement: There are a smooth function u and a smooth vector field X on Ω, smooth up to its one-sided boundary, with the following properties. (i) They satisfy u ≥ |X|g, u > 0 in int Ω, and (31.1) uµ + J(X) = 0. With symmetric indices denoting averaging, their equations are ∇(iXj) = −uKij, (31.2) ∆u = − divg K(X, ·)♯ , (31.3) ∇2 u = u(Ricg +τK − 2K2 ) − LXK + X(iJj). (31.4) Here Xi = gijXj and (K2)ij = KikKk j. (ii) On the chosen asymptotically flat end, (31.5) (u, X) = (b0 , b) + O2(r−q0 ). (iii) At the boundary, for the unit normal ν pointing into Ω, (31.6) X = uν, ∂νu + K(X, ν) = κ. Either u > 0 everywhere on S or u = 0 everywhere on S. (iv) On R × int Ω, set (31.7) g = −u2 dt2 + gij(dxi + Xi dt)(dxj + Xj dt), ξ = ∂t, N = u2 − |X|2 g. For the future normal n = u−1(ξ − X), the slice t = 0 has exactly the original induced metric g and second fundamental form K, with the convention of Theorem 22.4. Moreover, (31.8) Ricg(ξ, ·) = 0, Ricg = 0 on {N > 0}. (v) We have N ≥ 0, N → 1 at infinity, and N > 0 in a full collar just outside S. More precisely, in the positive boundary-lapse case, (31.9) N|S = 0, dN|S = 2uκ ν♭ = 2κX♭ . In the zero boundary-lapse case, if s ≥ 0 is the original g-normal distance from S, there are smooth one-sided fields d, Y2 such that (31.10) u = sd, X = s2 Y2, d|S = κ, N = s2 d2 − s2 |Y2|2 g  . Consequently all zeros of N in int Ω lie in a compact subset of that interior.
